text: Alex Russell first diagnosed this problem at Chrome Dev Summit in 2016 in a really amazing talk: [VIDEO] He makes the point that lots of JS frameworks are so large that you're already doomed before you write the first line of real "app code". The framework itself has already blown your performance budget.
Note that you should not choose Ember if you are creating an app intended to be used on mobile, as it doesn't yet have code-splitting. This talk explains about why this is a hard requirement: [VIDEO]

story: Things I learnt making a fast website
